claim: IBTrACS holds 13,635 storm systems; 8,457 reached tropical-storm strength (34 kt, NATURE TS, max wind of any agency); none has positions on both sides of the equator, at any strength
Records start in 1851 for storms at tropical-storm strength
34 knots is about 63 km/h; two thirds (68%) of storms first reach it 10-20 degrees from the equator; 40 of 8,457 (0.47%) within 5 degrees
NASA: textbooks say cyclones don't form within 300 km (about 186 miles) of the equator; 6 storms in the archive started within 3 degrees
evidence: NASA Earth Observatory 'A Rare Cyclone on the Equator' (2003), read 2026-11-16, quoted; hist bins 0-2

claim: Coriolis parameter f = 2 Omega sin(latitude); the ground turns about the local vertical once in 4 pi / f: 48 h at 30 deg, 92 h at 15 deg, 275 h at 5 deg, never at 0; sign flips across the equator
evidence: standard (Foucault pendulum period = sidereal day / sin latitude)

claim: Air drawn in from 500 km to 50 km, conserving absolute angular momentum, no friction: 0, 9, 32, 63, 93, 124 m/s at 0, 1.5, 5, 10, 15, 20 deg
evidence: spin.py exact formula v = f (R0^2 - r^2) / (2 r)

claim: Rotating axisymmetric shallow-water model, 600 km Gaussian dip at rest, c = 50 m/s, 4 days: dip kept 0, 0.2, 2.6, 8.3, 13.9, 21.0% at 0, 1.5, 5, 10, 15, 20 deg; linear Rossby-adjustment theory 0, 0.4, 2.7, 7.6, 13.2, 18.8%
evidence: adjust.py run 2026-11-16; theory = integral (r/L^2) K0(r/L) exp(-r^2/R0^2) dr

claim: Northern-hemisphere cyclones rotate anticlockwise, southern clockwise, because f changes sign
evidence: model sign (dv/dt = -f u with inflow u < 0); standard

claim: Closest at tropical-storm strength: Agni 2004 0.7N, Vamei 2001 1.5N, Sarah 1956 2.2N, unnamed 2024 2.2S, Alice 1979 2.5N, Peipah 2014 2.6N
Agni (JTWC IO052004): 35 kt at 0.7N on 28 Nov 2004, about 78 km from the equator (0.7 x 111 km); 65 kt by 2.7N on 29 Nov; IMD puts its formation near 1.5N
evidence: IBTrACS rows for SID 2004332N02072; IMD RSMC New Delhi 2004 report

claim: NASA on Vamei: topography and meteorology rather than Earth's rotation jump-started it; monsoon surge between the Malay Peninsula and Borneo; odds about once every 100 to 400 years (C.-P. Chang)
Beta drift: tropical cyclones drift poleward (and westward) because f changes with latitude
Limits: dry axisymmetric model, no convection, warm sea or shear; records thin before weather satellites (1960s)
Storms at tropical-storm strength by formation basin, 1851-2026: WP 2,223; NA 2,031; SI 1,416; EP 1,179; SP 834; NI 773; SA 1
evidence: basins.py over IBTrACS (same rule as tracks.py)

claim: Since 1980: 69% formed north of the equator; north peaks August-September, south peaks January-February

Catarina (March 2004, southern Brazil): NHC estimated category 1; first South Atlantic hurricane in the satellite record; IBTrACS has two more SA systems (2010, 2011) at 45 kt labelled DS (disturbance); NASA mentions further weak storms (e.g. Akara 2024) not in IBTrACS SA
evidence: NASA Earth Observatory 2024 quoted; IBTrACS rows 2004086S29318, 2010067S25317, 2011069S20321
